issues.title: Sign-reversed implicit trapezoidal inversion
issues.failure_explanation: Solving (1+x/2)/(1-x/2)=q gives x=2(q-1)/(q+1), whereas the old proof prints 2(1-q)/(1+q). For q=exp(i theta), the correct value is 2i tan(theta/2). The printed sign would imply the opposite rotation direction, and the subsequent factor 4 is also inconsistent. Thus the proof as written cannot establish the corollary's sign-preservation conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The conservative implicit-trapezoidal sign corollary is not proved as written, the old phase table is low by a factor of two, and the later dissipative corollary's referenced imaginary-sign argument inherits the faulty derivation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set q=exp(λh) and replace the inversion by hatλh=2(q−1)/(q+1). Then use Re(hatλh)=2(exp(2a)−1)/|q+1|² and Im(hatλh)=4exp(a)sin(θ)/|q+1|² for q=exp(a+iθ); in the conservative case this gives Im(hatλh)=2tan(θ/2). Apply these identities in the conservative proof, the phase table, and the dissipative corollary.
issues.why_classification: The printed proof relies on the sign-reversed expression and an inconsistent factor, so this is not merely transcriptional. The correct identities follow by short local algebra and preserve all hypotheses, sign conclusions, and the dependent corollary without a new lemma or substantive loss.

issues.title: RK3 dissipative conclusion has the wrong sign
issues.failure_explanation: Let q=exp(lambda h)=23/25 and choose delta=3/4. Then 6|1-q|=12/25 <= delta^2, q <= sqrt(8/9), and (6-delta^2)/(2delta)=29/8 >= sqrt(12.5), so the RK3 hypotheses hold. For p(z)=1+z+z^2/2+z^3/6, p(-0.1)<23/25<p(0), so a zero-loss root satisfying |z|<delta lies in (-0.1,0) and has negative real part. This contradicts the stated positive sign and agrees with the proof's own strong-damping analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary reverses the qualitative behavior of the selected RK3 learned root in its stated strongly damped regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the RK3 conclusion under the existing strong-damping hypotheses, replace Re(hatλ)>0 by Re(hatλ)<0, and make any summary of that same regime use the negative sign. No hypothesis or proof change is needed.
issues.why_classification: The old proof explicitly places the relevant bounded RK3 root in the left half-plane, and the surrounding conditional-dissipativity discussion agrees. Thus the old source uniquely forces the replacement of the isolated inequality sign, with no mathematical inference needing repair.

issues.title: Noisy one-step bound lacks a global inverse branch
issues.failure_explanation: The path hypothesis bounds |p| and |p'| pointwise but does not prevent rotation and cancellation in the segment average of (p^k)', nor does lambda* != hat(lambda) imply p(lambda*h)^k != p(hat(lambda)h)^k. For example, for the RK3 polynomial, p(0)=p(r)=1 with r=(-3+i sqrt(15))/2. Along the segment from 0 to r, p and p' have no zeros, so for every fixed finite data set a positive c_0 satisfying the stated finite-index condition exists. With zero noise, 0 and r are distinct global zero-loss minimizers, while the asserted estimate would force their distance to be zero. Thus the global parameter bound needs an inverse-branch selection that the old theorem lacks.
issues.overall_effect: The deterministic O(sigma) guarantee for an arbitrary global noisy minimizer is not established. The later LMM noise theorem also loses its only cited proof strategy, independently of its additional LMM-specific defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the estimate for a specified simple inverse branch: choose a noise-free root hatλ with p′(hatλh)≠0, select or constrain the noisy minimizer to a neighborhood on which the stacked forward map ξ↦(p(ξh)^k)_{k=1}^N is quantitatively injective, and prove the O(σ) estimate through a local inverse-function or lower-Lipschitz bound rather than the complex segment argument. The listed LMM dependency must likewise invoke only the analogous branch-local inverse principle.
issues.why_classification: Distinct global zero-loss roots are a natural feature of RK polynomials, so the arbitrary-global-minimizer guarantee cannot be retained by a routine technical edit. A branch-selected O(σ) perturbation theorem remains recognizably comparable and requires only a contained local inverse argument, so the repair entails limited quantifier loss but neither global reconstruction nor major loss.

issues.title: Reversed BDF2 characteristic numerator

failure_location.quote:
For the \textbf{BDF2} method, the expression is 
\[
\hat\lambda h = \frac{3 - 4\zeta + \zeta^2}{2\zeta^2}.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the BDF2 learned parameter is (3-4 zeta+zeta^2)/(2 zeta^2). The old coefficient table and Lemma 3.1 instead establish (1-4 zeta+3 zeta^2)/(2 zeta^2), equivalently (3 zeta^2-4 zeta+1)/(2 zeta^2). Reversing the constant and quadratic coefficients changes the repeated-root value from -1/6 to -1/2 and changes the conservative-data real-part conclusion to a nonnegative value.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed BDF2 parameter formula, its repeated-root entry, and its qualitative conservative-data discussion are wrong; the general LMM lemma remains valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Substitute the tabulated BDF2 coefficients into the general LMM formula and replace the display by hatλh=(3ζ²−4ζ+1)/(2ζ²). Recompute the repeated-root parameter as −1/2 and, for ζ=exp(iθ), record Re(hatλh)=(1−cosθ)²≥0; update the associated table entry and qualitative discussion. The general LMM lemma remains unchanged.
issues.why_classification: This is a short, source-forced coefficient substitution followed by elementary local recalculation. Because the repeated-root and sign discussion used the wrong formula, it is not a pure typo; nevertheless, the general result and the substantive conclusion that BDF2 can infer expansive behavior survive without a new argument or meaningful guarantee loss.

issues.title: False Leap–Frog admissible-region conclusion
issues.failure_explanation: Take lambda h = -log(2) + 2 pi i/3 and zero noise. Then zeta_2 = exp(lambda h) has modulus 1/2, zeta_1 = -exp(-lambda h) has modulus 2, and c_1=0, c_2=1 gives an exact zero-loss fit. The corresponding learned parameter is sinh(lambda h), whose real part is 3/8 > 0. It therefore lies in neither the asserted open left half-plane nor [-i,i]. The inference from stability of one characteristic root to the claimed region is false.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem does not guarantee that the Leap–Frog learned parameter is non-expansive; even admissible noiseless data from a damped mode can produce a learned parameter in the right half-plane.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the claimed left-half-plane-or-segment conclusion. In the noiseless case replace it by the exact identity hatλh=sinh(λh); writing λh=a+iθ with a<0 gives Re(hatλh)=sinh(a)cos(θ), which is negative only when cos(θ)>0 and can be positive otherwise. Any retained non-expansivity statement must therefore add a corresponding phase restriction, such as |θ|<π/2 on the principal range, and no unconditional noisy-data region claim follows from the existence of one stable characteristic root alone.
issues.why_classification: The stable-root premise imposes no left-half-plane restriction, and the counterexample lies in a natural damped oscillatory regime. Every valid repair either removes the theorem’s central non-expansivity guarantee or excludes a substantial phase regime, so the affected result suffers major mathematical loss even though the correcting algebra is local.

issues.title: Adams–Bashforth scaled-parameter order overstated
issues.failure_explanation: For AB2, set x=lambda h and zeta=exp(x). Expanding 2(zeta^2-zeta)/(3zeta-1) gives hat(lambda)h = x + (5/12)x^3 + O(x^4). For fixed nonzero lambda, the error is therefore of order h^3, whereas the theorem's k=2 bullet claims order h^4. In general the scaled AB error should be O(h^(k+1)), not O(h^(k+2)).
issues.overall_effect: The theorem overstates Adams–Bashforth recovery accuracy by one power of h; its Adams–Moulton and Leap–Frog bullets are not affected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Adams–Bashforth bullet by |λh−hatλh|=O(h^(k+1)), equivalently |hatλ−λ|=O(h^k). Amend the proof with the corresponding Taylor expansion—for AB2, hatλh=x+(5/12)x³+O(x⁴)—while leaving the Adams–Moulton and Leap–Frog bullets unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained Taylor calculation, but it worsens the stated Adams–Bashforth rate by one full power of h and therefore withdraws a coherent substantive rate guarantee. The same convergence theorem and method class survive with only this limited loss, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.
